Good for testing the weapon. Now work on BRASS (breath, relax, aim, squeeze, shoot). You pulled the trigger on most of them instead of squeezing it, and the there are a couple where you failed to control your breathing.

Your shot groups should be as consistent and as small as possible, and for an ar-15 it should be within centimeters of each other. The rifle looks like it is zeroed wrong? Or maybe you just pull most of your shots, but either way it looks like the center of you shot grouping is to the right of center mass, so it looks like you need to adjust the rear sight appature, or better control your trigger pull. You shouldn't be using Kentucky windage to hit the target, always aim center mass and adjust the sights, not your aim.

Your technique should be as consistent as possible, the position you put your head on the rifle to aim should always be the same, so I would always recommend putting your nose against the charging handle when you aim. And choose the same breathing position, so either you breath in and hold your breath when you shoot, but I would recommend you exhale and then hold your breath and shoot, reason for this is it feels to me that there is less pressure to me and I think it is more consistent than the other way. Some people recommend stop in the middle of your in breath and then hold it, but I think it is too inconsistent that is why I recommend the other two.

The shot should come as a surprise, what I mean by this is that, you should slowly squeeze the trigger until the rifle surprises you by going off. It is a mistake to simply pull the trigger, as it is poor technique and will lead to wider shot groups. You should use the very end pad of your trigger finger, although you can still use the middle of your finger, using the end pad will lead to you pulling the shot less, and should lead to tighter shot groups. And definitely do not use the crease of a knuckle, always use the meat of the pad.

The last piece of advise is always return to the basics. You can develop poor habits and develop a sense of arrogance from experience, saying "I already know how to shoot, I dont need to listen to this", but even after shooting for so long it is likely that you will simply have forgotten to do the small things.
